label: Self-giving is also efficient self-causation under the selected causal sense
term: bridge between time-indexed self-giving and efficient self-causation
definition: SelfGivingIsEfficientSelfCause F EfficientlyCausesIn means: for each world v, candidate c and moment t, if F.GivesAt v c c t (c exercises concurrent giving of its own esse at t) then EfficientlyCausesIn c c F.esse. The target is a distinct supplied efficient-cause relation in a particular respect, not F.CausesIn (cause of a perfection) or a vague causal-power predicate. The bridge only constrains the potential self-case and is weaker than the full relation inclusion for all c,x. Its independent applicability is a substantive OPEN causal interpretation.
note: The priority argument being imported is Aquinas's already verified Second Way no-self-cause derivation. Its priority sense is F.PriorSimply, not chronological order; the bridge is a conditional meaning link rather than a new source attribution. The selfGivingFrame control retains both priority premises while falsifying this bridge and no-self-giving.
